title: My PhD Interview at Isfahan University of Technology
excerpt: My PhD interview at Isfahan University of Technology went well and I was accepted as the top pick, but I turned it down. Here's why.

blocks.text: Very well. This time I'm going to talk about my PhD interview at Isfahan University of Technology. First of all, I need to say that the PhD interview I was supposed to have at the University of Technology was on exactly the same day as the Shahid Beheshti University PhD interview. So I didn't go to Isfahan University of Technology and preferred Shahid Beheshti in Tehran. But they called me and set up a late round interview, or one for those who went late, and I was actually in the second period of time there.

I honestly don't remember the time that was announced, but I think I entered their computer engineering faculty half an hour or an hour early again and waited behind the door. They had chosen a classroom, it was a relatively small class, I don't remember, it was a class or a lab. One person had gone into the interview before me and I waited for that person to come out.

One of the bad things here was that it wasn't clear at all who was who, we had to figure it out ourselves and tick our names in front of them, things like that. But when it was my turn I entered, and I think about 6-7 of their professors were sitting there.

I had applied to the University of Technology for both Software and its Artificial Intelligence, I was accepted for both but I only went for Software. Just like the University of Isfahan I only went for Software, I'm not that interested in AI.

When the interview started they asked me to introduce myself. I gave a short introduction of myself, who I am, what path I came on, and what things I've done up to today, and then they started asking questions. I also gave the forms I had given them one by one to each of them and they were very surprised, like they had really never seen such things in their lives.

One point the University of Technology had was that we chose our favorite professor beforehand and I had also chosen, and they asked me in the session why I chose him and I said the reason, because his field was closer to me, but the reality is that none of those professors had that same field as me.

The interview session went well. They asked about my father's and mother's jobs, they also asked a series of belief and political questions, unlike everywhere, which in my opinion professionally and ethically there's no place for such questions in a PhD interview session and asking such questions is professionally ugly. And I naturally answered those questions, but the answer I gave was a very vague answer, meaning for example I would say it doesn't matter to me what politics is in power or whatever else, and the reality is also the same.

In the end when the interview finished, I myself was satisfied and I felt I would be accepted and fortunately I was accepted. That same professor called me and said you were chosen as the top pick and first, and what's your decision? In the end I decided to reject this opportunity.

The biggest reasons I had for rejecting this PhD opportunity: first was that the way to the University of Technology was very far from us and commuting was very hard. And well, at the University of Isfahan I had much easier commuting.
Naturally the second reason was the excessive and unnecessary strictness I had heard the professors there have.

The third reason was the weakness of academic work in that faculty of mine, Software. I mean when I checked the professors' Scholar, for example each one had only one or two papers, and for maybe the past five or six years. And I didn't see any scientific research activity from these people, that they work on papers or submit papers. Although I don't have information about what projects they have going on and the practical work they do. But the scientific and research work that was very important to me, they naturally weren't doing.

And the last reason, which was a very important reason for me, was that the field I'm focusing on, which is now AI Agent and Small Language Model and these kinds of things, was far from the thinking of these professors and they liked to change my field and take me towards Human-Computer Interaction. And for this reason I ultimately decided to reject this opportunity and I hope it was the right decision.
